result.title: Finite-Memory Control of POMDPs: Fundamental Limits and Efficient Design
result.summary: Optimal control of partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs), in general, requires a complete history. The belief state, a distribution over hidden states, summarizes this history and provides the classical sufficient statistic to control POMDPs. However, the continuous nature of the belief space generally prevents a finite-memory controller from maintaining it exactly. This raises the question we address in this work: what must the available finite memory preserve to achieve near-optimal control performance? We study this question through an information-theoretic converse that gives a fundamental lower bound on the loss of any finite-memory controller. The analysis introduces the concept of a decision witness that characterizes belief states whose confusion would lead to unavoidable loss. Motivated by this bound, we propose RECAP, a constructive quantization method for designing representative memory states. We prove an upper bound on the optimality gap of any RECAP codebook and use the components of this bound together with the converse analysis to define the codebook objective. Experiments on 11 POMDP benchmarks demonstrate that RECAP improves over finite-memory representation baselines under the same memory budget.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究有限记忆 POMDP 控制器必须保留信念状态的哪些信息才能接近最优，给出有限记忆控制器损失的信息论下界，提出刻画「混淆即致损」的 decision witness 概念，并据此设计 RECAP 量化码本方法，在 11 个 POMDP 基准上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「哪些信念混淆会导致不可避免损失」的刻画与码本量化，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态应保留哪些视觉证据、如何度量信息坍缩与状态抽象粒度提供可供核查的分析参照。
